header.scope: In-process engine execution only: the deterministic engine called as a function in one Node process, on one thread.
excludedFromTiming: the ledger write (no decision record is stored)
connector calls (inputs are generated in-process; the connector is declared, never called)
request generation (built before the timer starts)
warm-up decisions (the warm variant runs 2,000 untimed first)
header.notM1OrM2: This is NOT M1 or M2. ADR-016 §7 defines M1 as the built decision service over HTTP with open-loop load for at least 30 minutes, and M2 as that with the synchronous ledger write at 10M and 100M decision records. Neither has been measured, and no script exists for either.
header.machine: 12 logical cores, 15.8 GB, win32 10.0.26220 x64, Node v20.19.3
header.machineLoad: Not controlled: a developer machine with other processes running. In this run the warm variant's p99 exceeded the cold variant's, which a quiet machine would not produce; treat the spread between runs as noise of that size.
header.tenant: 'bench' — a synthetic tenant generated by bench/datasets. Not the demo tenant (telco-us) and not its catalogue.
header.dataset: Synthetic, seeded: 100 active offers, 3 targeting policies with each offer scoped by 2, 1 frequency policy, 1 boost, 1 declared connector. Requests are drawn from 1,000,000 distinct generated customer ids; there is no profile store, so no decision reads a profile from storage.
requestMix: One flow: source, eligibility filter, relevance filter, frequency constraint, score node, arbitrate.
Channel cycles deterministically over web, email, sms, push and outbound_call; one placement.
Customer attributes (segment, tenure, credit score, spend, active) are seeded per customer id.
The score node pins a model id, and its propensity is a seeded hash of customer, offer and model — no model runs.
cacheStates: S1-cold: no warm-up, first decisions of the process
header.generalisesTo: Only this: in-process engine cost for one tenant with 100 active offers, on the machine above. Not a service latency, not throughput under concurrent load, not a figure for any other catalogue size or tenant.

notMeasured.reason: There is no online feature service, so a miss rate would be a number about nothing.
Connector resolution runs before the deterministic core by design, so the harness would be timing a stub rather than a degraded dependency.
notMeasured.blockedOn: W-010, and the gateway entering the measured path

notMeasured.reason: Measured and published on every variant, never gated. It swings 3x with machine load, and a gate that flaps is one people learn to ignore. The number is in the result so a regression is still visible.
notMeasured.blockedOn: nothing — this is a decision, not a gap

notMeasured.reason: This harness is single-threaded and measures per-core capacity. A service-level throughput claim needs the service, not the engine, and holding one to the other would compare two different things.
notMeasured.blockedOn: a deployed service under load, not this harness
